text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Sali Berisha and the government are in a very difficult position as they seek to return the money to depositors of failed pyramid schemes.

- Opposition Socialist leader Rexhep Mejdani accuses the ruling Democratic Party of setting up a de-facto state of emergency after the government arrests numerous people it accuses of taking part in violent weekend protests.
- Albanian police broke up an anti-government rally called by Azem Hajdari, head of a trade union and one of the leaders of a 1990 revolt which toppled the former communist regime.
- A group of intellectuals calls on the people to continue peaceful protests against the Democratic Party which they blame for the crisis situation in the country.
- Some branches of the Democratic Party calls for more counter-demonstrations.
- Lek significantly devalued on Wednesday, with $1 now worth 123 leks compared with around 114 lek the day before.
- World Bank representative Carlos Elbirt says they cannot finance half-pyramid half-investment companies.
- Appeals court reduces the jail sentences for Irakli Kocollari and Vladimir Hysi, former senior police officials who were imprisoned for abuse of power and perjury.
- Vefa Holding, the largest pyramid/investment scheme, does not give depositors returns in hard currency.
- Hundreds of Albanians arrested in the country charged with damaging government buildings in recent protests.
- Berisha proposes giving depositors with failed pyramid schemes bank certificates rather than hard cash.
- Seven left and right-wing opposition parties create the Forum of Democracy which calls for government resignation and investigation into savings schemes.
